spec.description: Fleet overview and per-host details for Windows hosts monitored by windows_exporter.
Windows product name and version reported by the os collector. Use this to distinguish hosts when investigating version-specific behavior.
spec.title: Operating system

spec.description: Time each collector spent per scrape. Compare against the scrape timeout.
spec.title: Collector duration

spec.description: Collectors that failed at least once in the selected time range.
spec.title: Collector failures

spec.description: Collectors that hit the collector timeout at least once in the selected time range.
spec.title: Collector timeouts

spec.description: CPU time used by the exporter process, as a share of one core. CPU usage grows with the number of scrapes, for example when two Prometheus jobs scrape the same exporter; CPU per scrape (right axis) does not.
spec.title: Exporter CPU usage

spec.description: Working set and private bytes of the exporter process, and the Go heap in use. Steady growth points to a leak.
spec.title: Exporter memory

spec.description: Open handles of the exporter process (process_open_fds). Steady growth points to a handle leak.
spec.title: Exporter handles

spec.description: Steady growth of goroutines points to a goroutine leak. Goroutines that stay "not in Go" sit in a system call, for example a collector waiting on WMI or PDH. The states need an exporter build with the Go scheduler metrics; the total line works with every build.
spec.title: Goroutines by state

spec.description: Goroutines started per second, and OS threads owned by the Go runtime. Goroutines created needs an exporter build with the Go scheduler metrics.
spec.title: Goroutines created and threads

spec.description: Time goroutines wait in the runnable state before they run. High values mean the exporter does not get enough CPU. Needs an exporter build with the Go scheduler metrics.
spec.title: Scheduler latency

spec.description: Time since the last boot.
spec.title: Uptime

spec.description: Average GC pause and GC runs per second.
spec.title: Garbage collection

spec.description: Bytes allocated on the Go heap per second. Spikes line up with expensive collectors.
spec.title: Allocation rate

spec.description: Number of logical processors available to Windows, including SMT threads. This is the logical CPU count rather than the number of physical sockets.
spec.title: CPUs

spec.expr: max by (luid, phys) (windows_gpu_temperature_celsius{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

max by (luid, phys) (windows_gpu_temperature_warning_celsius{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

max by (luid, phys) (windows_gpu_temperature_max_celsius{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

spec.description: Current GPU temperature, driver-reported throttling threshold and maximum temperature in degrees Celsius. Sustained readings near the warning threshold can indicate insufficient cooling. Requires the gpu collector, WDDM 2.4 or newer and driver support. Unsupported sensor values are absent, rather than zero.
spec.title: GPU temperature

spec.expr: max by (luid, phys) (windows_gpu_fan_speed_rpm{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

max by (luid, phys) (windows_gpu_fan_speed_max_rpm{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

spec.description: Current and maximum main-fan speed in revolutions per minute. A supported fan can report zero when stopped under light load. Requires the gpu collector, WDDM 2.4 or newer and driver support. Unsupported sensor values are absent, rather than zero.
spec.title: GPU fan speed

spec.expr: max by (luid, phys) (windows_gpu_power_usage_ratio{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

spec.description: Current GPU power draw as a fraction of the driver-reported maximum power (TDP). This is a ratio, not an absolute measurement in watts. Requires the gpu collector, WDDM 2.4 or newer and driver support. Unsupported sensor values are absent, rather than zero.
spec.title: GPU power usage

spec.expr: max by (luid, phys) (windows_gpu_memory_frequency_hertz{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

max by (luid, phys) (windows_gpu_memory_frequency_max_hertz{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

spec.description: Current and maximum non-overclocked GPU memory clock in hertz. Clocks can fall at idle; correlate drops under load with temperature and power. Requires the gpu collector, WDDM 2.4 or newer and driver support. Unsupported sensor values are absent, rather than zero.
spec.title: GPU memory clock

spec.expr: max by (luid, phys, eng) (windows_gpu_engine_frequency_hertz{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

max by (luid, phys, eng) (windows_gpu_engine_frequency_max_hertz{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

spec.description: Current and maximum non-overclocked frequency per GPU engine in hertz. Only engines with a reported maximum clock are exposed, typically the 3D engine. Requires the gpu collector, WDDM 2.4 or newer and driver support. Unsupported sensor values are absent, rather than zero.
spec.title: GPU engine clock

spec.expr: max by (luid, phys) (windows_gpu_adapter_memory_committed_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

spec.description: Total committed GPU memory per physical GPU in bytes. Commitment is a separate accounting measure from dedicated or shared memory residency; do not add these series together.
spec.title: GPU committed memory

spec.expr: sum by (luid, phys) (windows_gpu_local_adapter_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

sum by (luid, phys) (windows_gpu_non_local_adapter_memory_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid, phys) group_left (name) max by (luid, phys, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

spec.description: Local and non-local adapter memory usage in bytes, summed across memory partitions for each physical GPU. These describe memory locality and overlap the dedicated/shared accounting views.
spec.title: GPU local and non-local memory

spec.expr: max by (luid) (windows_gpu_dedicated_system_memory_size_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid) group_left (name) max by (luid, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

spec.description: System memory dedicated to each GPU in bytes. This capacity is distinct from dedicated video memory and the shared system memory pool; it can be zero on discrete adapters.
spec.title: GPU dedicated system memory capacity

spec.expr: topk(10, (sum by (process_id) (windows_gpu_process_memory_shared_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (process_id) group_left (process) max by (process_id, process) (windows_process_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})) or on (process_id) sum by (process_id) (windows_gpu_process_memory_shared_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}))

spec.description: Top ten processes at each point in time by shared GPU memory in bytes, summed across GPUs. Membership can change over time. Process names require the process collector; otherwise the PID is shown. Memory accounting views overlap and should not be added together.
spec.title: Top 10 processes by shared GPU memory

spec.expr: topk(10, (sum by (process_id) (windows_gpu_process_memory_committed_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (process_id) group_left (process) max by (process_id, process) (windows_process_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})) or on (process_id) sum by (process_id) (windows_gpu_process_memory_committed_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}))

spec.description: Top ten processes at each point in time by committed GPU memory in bytes, summed across GPUs. Membership can change over time. Process names require the process collector; otherwise the PID is shown. Memory accounting views overlap and should not be added together.
spec.title: Top 10 processes by committed GPU memory

spec.description: Total physical memory visible to Windows in bytes. Compare with used memory and commit charge when investigating memory pressure.
spec.title: RAM

spec.expr: topk(10, (sum by (process_id) (windows_gpu_process_memory_local_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (process_id) group_left (process) max by (process_id, process) (windows_process_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})) or on (process_id) sum by (process_id) (windows_gpu_process_memory_local_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}))

spec.description: Top ten processes at each point in time by local GPU memory in bytes, summed across GPUs. Membership can change over time. Process names require the process collector; otherwise the PID is shown. Memory accounting views overlap and should not be added together.
spec.title: Top 10 processes by local GPU memory

spec.expr: topk(10, (sum by (process_id) (windows_gpu_process_memory_non_local_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (process_id) group_left (process) max by (process_id, process) (windows_process_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})) or on (process_id) sum by (process_id) (windows_gpu_process_memory_non_local_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}))

spec.description: Top ten processes at each point in time by non-local GPU memory in bytes, summed across GPUs. Membership can change over time. Process names require the process collector; otherwise the PID is shown. Memory accounting views overlap and should not be added together.
spec.title: Top 10 processes by non-local GPU memory

spec.description: Percentage of non-idle CPU time averaged across logical processors over the rate interval. Sustained high values together with a growing processor queue can indicate CPU contention.
spec.title: CPU busy

spec.description: Needs the tcp collector, which is not enabled by default. A growing CLOSE_WAIT count means an application does not close its sockets. Many TIME_WAIT connections can use up the dynamic port range for outgoing connections.
spec.title: TCP connections by state

spec.description: Outgoing (active) and incoming (passive) connections opened per second, connection attempts that failed, and established connections that were reset.
spec.title: TCP connections opened, failed and reset

spec.description: Received segments are drawn below the axis.
spec.title: TCP segments

spec.description: Retransmitted segments as a share of sent segments. A rate that stays above a few percent points to packet loss on the network.
spec.title: TCP retransmission rate

spec.description: Needs the udp collector, which is not enabled by default. Received datagrams are drawn below the axis.
spec.title: UDP datagrams

spec.description: Received datagrams that could not be delivered, and datagrams for a port that no application listens on.
spec.title: UDP errors

spec.description: Percentage of physical memory in use, calculated as total minus available memory. This differs from commit charge, which measures promised virtual memory against the commit limit.
spec.title: Memory used

spec.description: Committed virtual memory as a share of the commit limit (physical memory + page files). Allocations fail at 100%.
spec.title: Commit used

spec.expr: count(windows_service_state{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", state="running"} == 0 and on (name) windows_service_start_mode{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", start_mode="auto"} == 1) or vector(0)

spec.description: Services with start mode "auto" that are not running. See the Services tab for names.
spec.title: Stopped auto services

spec.description: Percentage of non-idle CPU time averaged across logical processors. This measures CPU time rather than the frequency-adjusted processor utility shown by Windows Task Manager.
spec.title: CPU utilization

spec.description: Available memory is the standby (cache), free and zero page lists.
spec.title: Physical memory

spec.expr: (max by (instance, product, version) (windows_os_info{job=~"$job"})) and on (instance) windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}
(100 * (1 - avg by (instance) (clamp_max(rate(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"$job", mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval]), 1)))) and on (instance) windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}

(max by (instance) (100 * (1 - windows_logical_disk_free_bytes{job=~"$job", volume!~"HarddiskVolume.*"} / windows_logical_disk_size_bytes{job=~"$job", volume!~"HarddiskVolume.*"}))) and on (instance) windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}
(sum by (instance) (windows_service_state{job=~"$job", state="running"})) and on (instance) windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}

(count by (instance) (windows_service_state{job=~"$job", state="running"} == 0 and on (instance, name) windows_service_start_mode{job=~"$job", start_mode="auto"} == 1)) and on (instance) windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}

spec.description: One row per scraped host. Click a hostname to open its details. Services up counts running services; Auto stopped counts services with start mode auto that are not running.
spec.title: Hosts

spec.description: Size, available space and used percentage of each selected logical volume. Windows free-space counters can lag by 10 to 15 minutes; use trends rather than treating a single sample as immediate confirmation of reclaimed space.
spec.title: Volumes

spec.description: Sum over the selected volumes. Reads are drawn below the axis.
spec.title: Disk throughput

spec.description: Sum over the selected interfaces. Received traffic is drawn below the axis.
spec.title: Network throughput

spec.expr: sum by (mode) (rate(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", mode!="idle"}[$__rate_interval])) / scalar(count(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", mode="idle"}))

spec.description: Share of total CPU time across all logical processors.
spec.title: CPU utilization by mode

spec.description: Busy time of each logical processor, labelled processor group,core. Green is idle, red is fully busy.
spec.title: CPU utilization per core

spec.description: Threads that are ready to run but waiting for a CPU. A sustained value above 2 per core indicates CPU contention.
spec.title: Processor queue length

spec.description: Context switches, hardware interrupts and deferred procedure calls per second across the host. High rates can reflect scheduling or driver activity; correlate changes with CPU usage and workload rather than assuming they are faults.
spec.title: Context switches and interrupts

spec.description: Current process and thread counts on the host. Sustained growth can help identify runaway process creation or thread leaks; thread counts use the right-hand axis.
spec.title: Processes and threads

spec.description: System calls and exception dispatches per second. Exception dispatches include handled exceptions and do not directly count application crashes; compare with application logs. Exceptions use the right-hand axis.
spec.title: System calls and exceptions

spec.expr: topk(25, (100 * (1 - avg by (instance) (clamp_max(rate(windows_cpu_time_total{job=~"$job", mode="idle"}[$__rate_interval]), 1)))) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

spec.description: Shows the 25 highest hosts at each point in time.
spec.title: CPU utilization

spec.description: Effective frequency from the APERF/MPERF counters, averaged and maximum across logical processors, against the nominal frequency. Values above nominal mean turbo boost.
spec.title: CPU frequency

spec.description: Available memory is the standby (cache), free and zero page lists.
spec.title: Physical memory

spec.description: Committed virtual memory against the commit limit (physical memory + page files).
spec.title: Commit charge

spec.description: Hard page faults read from or written to disk. Sustained page reads indicate memory pressure.
spec.title: Paging

spec.description: A steadily growing nonpaged pool usually means a driver leaks memory.
spec.title: Kernel pools and cache

spec.description: Size, available space and used percentage of each selected logical volume. Windows free-space counters can lag by 10 to 15 minutes; use trends rather than treating a single sample as immediate confirmation of reclaimed space.
spec.title: Volumes

spec.description: Used space as a percentage of each selected logical volume. Sustained growth toward full capacity can prevent writes and disrupt applications; Windows free-space counters can lag by 10 to 15 minutes.
spec.title: Volume usage

spec.description: Share of time the volume was servicing requests (1 - idle time).
spec.title: Volume busy time

spec.expr: topk(25, (max by (instance) (100 * (1 - windows_memory_physical_free_bytes{job=~"$job"} / windows_memory_physical_total_bytes{job=~"$job"}))) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

spec.description: Shows the 25 highest hosts at each point in time.
spec.title: Memory utilization

spec.description: Reads are drawn below the axis.
spec.title: Disk throughput

spec.description: Reads are drawn below the axis.
spec.title: Disk IOPS

spec.description: Average time per read and write operation. Reads are drawn below the axis.
spec.title: Disk latency

spec.description: Average number of read and write requests queued for the volume. Reads are drawn below the axis. A queue that stays high while latency rises indicates a disk bottleneck. The avg_*_requests_queued metrics grow like counters, so the panel takes their rate.
spec.title: Disk queue length

spec.description: Received traffic is drawn below the axis.
spec.title: Network throughput

spec.description: Sent plus received traffic relative to the link speed reported by the adapter. Interfaces without a link speed are not shown.
spec.title: Network utilization

spec.description: Received packets are drawn below the axis.
spec.title: Packets

spec.description: Receive and transmit packet errors, discarded packets and received packets with unknown protocols per second for each selected interface. Errors can indicate link or driver problems; discards can reflect buffer pressure or filtering.
spec.title: Network errors and discards

spec.expr: topk(25, (max by (instance) (100 * (1 - windows_logical_disk_free_bytes{job=~"$job", volume!~"HarddiskVolume.*"} / windows_logical_disk_size_bytes{job=~"$job", volume!~"HarddiskVolume.*"}))) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

spec.description: Usage of the fullest volume per host. Shows the 25 highest hosts at each point in time.
spec.title: Fullest volume

spec.description: Number of services currently in the running state, reported by the service collector. Compare unexpected drops with the stopped automatic services table and service change history.
spec.title: Running services

spec.expr: count(windows_service_state{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", state="running"} == 0 and on (name) windows_service_start_mode{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", start_mode="auto"} == 1) or vector(0)

spec.description: Services with start mode "auto" that are not running.
spec.title: Stopped auto services

spec.expr: sum(windows_service_state{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", state=~".* pending"}) or vector(0)

spec.description: Services in a start, stop, pause or continue pending state. A service that stays pending is hung.
spec.title: Pending services

spec.description: Number of services configured with disabled startup. A disabled service cannot start until its startup mode changes; disabled services are not necessarily unhealthy.
spec.title: Disabled services

spec.expr: max by (name, state) (windows_service_state{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"} == 1) and on (name) (windows_service_state{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", state="running"} == 0) and on (name) (windows_service_start_mode{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", start_mode="auto"} == 1)

spec.description: Services configured to start automatically that are not in the running state. Delayed-start and trigger-start services may show up here until they start.
spec.title: Automatic services not running

spec.expr: windows_service_state{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", state="running"} and on (name) (changes(windows_service_state{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", state="running"}[$__range] @ end()) > 0)

spec.description: Services that started or stopped in the selected time range.
spec.title: Service state changes

spec.description: Needs the gpu collector, which is not enabled by default. Utilization is the busiest engine of the GPU.
spec.title: GPUs

spec.expr: clamp_max(max by (luid, engtype) (sum by (luid, eng, engtype) (rate(windows_gpu_engine_time_seconds{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))), 1) * on (luid) group_left (name) max by (luid, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

spec.description: Busiest engine of each engine type, as in Task Manager.
spec.title: GPU utilization by engine type

spec.expr: max by (luid) (windows_gpu_adapter_memory_dedicated_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid) group_left (name) max by (luid, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

max by (luid) (windows_gpu_dedicated_video_memory_size_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid) group_left (name) max by (luid, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})
max by (luid) (windows_gpu_adapter_memory_shared_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid) group_left (name) max by (luid, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})
max by (luid) (windows_gpu_shared_system_memory_size_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (luid) group_left (name) max by (luid, name) (windows_gpu_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})

spec.description: Dedicated (video) and shared (system) memory in use, against the size of each pool.
spec.title: GPU memory

spec.expr: topk(25, (sum by (instance) (rate(windows_net_bytes_sent_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8)) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

topk(25, (sum by (instance) (rate(windows_net_bytes_received_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval]) * 8)) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

spec.description: Sum over all interfaces. Received is drawn below the axis. Shows the 25 highest hosts at each point in time.
spec.title: Network throughput

spec.expr: topk(10, (max by (process_id) (sum by (process_id, luid, eng) (rate(windows_gpu_engine_time_seconds{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on (process_id) group_left (process) max by (process_id, process) (windows_process_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})) or on (process_id) max by (process_id) (sum by (process_id, luid, eng) (rate(windows_gpu_engine_time_seconds{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))))

spec.description: Busiest GPU engine used by each process. Process names need the process collector; otherwise only the PID is shown.
spec.title: Top 10 processes by GPU utilization

spec.expr: topk(10, (sum by (process_id) (windows_gpu_process_memory_dedicated_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}) * on (process_id) group_left (process) max by (process_id, process) (windows_process_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"})) or on (process_id) sum by (process_id) (windows_gpu_process_memory_dedicated_bytes{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}))

spec.description: Process names need the process collector; otherwise only the PID is shown.
spec.title: Top 10 processes by dedicated GPU memory

spec.description: Needs the hyperv collector, which is not enabled by default.
spec.title: Virtual machines

spec.description: Number of Hyper-V virtual machines reporting critical health. Inspect the affected VM and Hyper-V event logs; this requires the optional hyperv collector.
spec.title: VMs in critical health

spec.description: Whether the Hyper-V WMI namespace answers. When it stops answering, Hyper-V Manager and Failover Cluster Manager usually cannot manage the host.
spec.title: Hyper-V WMI

spec.description: Number of host logical processors reported by Hyper-V. Use this as capacity context for host and virtual processor load; this requires the optional hyperv collector.
spec.title: Logical processors

spec.description: Virtual processors assigned to all VMs.
spec.title: Virtual processors

spec.description: Virtual processors assigned to VMs per logical processor of the host.
spec.title: vCPU per logical CPU

spec.expr: sum by (state) (rate(windows_hyperv_hypervisor_logical_processor_time_total{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", state!="idle"}[$__rate_interval])) / scalar(count(windows_hyperv_hypervisor_logical_processor_time_total{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", state="idle"}))

spec.description: Share of all logical processors spent running guest code (VMs and the root partition) and in the hypervisor. With Hyper-V enabled, the CPU tab only sees the root partition.
spec.title: Host CPU time by state

spec.expr: topk(25, (sum by (instance) (rate(windows_logical_disk_write_bytes_total{job=~"$job", volume!~"HarddiskVolume.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

topk(25, (sum by (instance) (rate(windows_logical_disk_read_bytes_total{job=~"$job", volume!~"HarddiskVolume.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

spec.description: Sum over all volumes. Read is drawn below the axis. Shows the 25 highest hosts at each point in time.
spec.title: Disk throughput

spec.description: Virtual processor run time of each VM as a share of all logical processors of the host.
spec.title: CPU usage per VM

spec.description: Physical memory currently assigned to each VM with dynamic memory.
spec.title: Memory assigned to VMs

spec.description: Memory a VM needs as a share of the memory it has. Above 100% the VM needs more memory than it is assigned.
spec.title: VM memory pressure

spec.description: Memory the dynamic memory balancer can still hand out to VMs.
spec.title: Memory available for VMs

spec.description: Reads are drawn below the axis.
spec.title: Virtual disk throughput

spec.description: Reads are drawn below the axis.
spec.title: Virtual disk IOPS

spec.description: Average I/O latency of each virtual disk. windows_hyperv_virtual_storage_device_latency_seconds holds the raw, growing counter in 100 ns ticks, so the panel divides its rate by the rate of I/O operations. Errors use the right axis.
spec.title: Virtual disk latency and errors

spec.expr: topk(25, (sum by (instance) (rate(windows_net_packets_received_errors_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(windows_net_packets_received_discarded_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(windows_net_packets_outbound_errors_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval]) + rate(windows_net_packets_outbound_discarded_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval]))) * on (instance) group_left (hostname) max by (instance, hostname) (windows_os_hostname{job=~"$job", hostname=~"$hostname"}))

spec.description: Sum over all interfaces of received and outbound errors and discards. Shows the 25 highest hosts at each point in time.
spec.title: Network errors and discards

spec.description: Received traffic is drawn below the axis.
spec.title: Virtual switch throughput

spec.description: Incoming and outgoing packets dropped per second by each Hyper-V virtual switch. Correlate sustained drops with network load, resource pressure and switch policies; this requires the optional hyperv collector.
spec.title: Virtual switch dropped packets

spec.description: Received traffic is drawn below the axis.
spec.title: VM network adapter throughput

spec.description: Needs the time collector, which is not enabled by default.
spec.title: Time zone

spec.description: Active Windows Time synchronization provider. A non-NTP provider can be expected on virtual machines; this requires the optional time collector.
spec.title: Clock sync source

spec.description: Number of time sources the NTP client uses. 0 means the clock is not synchronized.
spec.title: NTP time sources

spec.description: Absolute offset between the system clock and the selected time source.
spec.title: Clock offset

spec.description: Signed offset from the selected time source and the NTP request round-trip delay, in seconds. Persistent offset or increased delay can affect time-sensitive applications; this compares the host to its chosen source and does not independently verify that source.
spec.title: Clock offset and NTP round-trip delay

spec.description: Result of the last scrape by Prometheus.
spec.title: Scrape status

spec.expr: windows_exporter_build_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance", version!=""} or on (instance) label_replace(windows_exporter_build_info{job=~"$job", instance="$instance"}, "version", "$1", "revision", "(.{7}).*")

spec.description: Builds without a version show the first seven characters of the Git revision.
spec.title: Exporter version

spec.description: Time since the exporter process started. A short uptime on a host with a long uptime means the exporter restarted.
spec.title: Exporter uptime

spec.description: Number of collectors that failed on the latest scrape, including timeouts. The graph shows the count over the selected time range.
spec.title: Failed collectors

spec.description: Number of collectors that timed out on the latest scrape. The graph shows the count over the selected time range.
spec.title: Timed-out collectors

spec.description: Number of metric samples returned before Prometheus metric relabeling. Changes can reflect collector configuration or changing device/process counts; unexpected drops should be checked against scrape and collector success.
spec.title: Samples per scrape

spec.description: Scrape duration measured by Prometheus and by the exporter. It must stay below the scrape timeout of the job.
spec.title: Scrape duration

spec.description: Scrape requests by HTTP status code, and errors while gathering or encoding metrics. More requests than one per scrape interval mean several jobs or Prometheus servers scrape this exporter.
spec.title: HTTP requests to /metrics

spec.description: Latest success, timeout and duration for each enabled collector. Success is 1 for a completed collection and 0 for a failure; timeout is 1 when the scrape budget was exceeded. Disabled collectors are absent.
spec.title: Collectors
